definition: A programming language that compiles to JavaScript and offers concise functional syntax.
example: A developer pipes input through a sequence of transformations.

definition: An educational programming language known for turtle graphics and procedures.
example: A student turns and advances a turtle to draw a square.

definition: A lightweight scripting language designed to embed in host programs.
example: A game designer uses a Lua script to respond to an in-game event.

definition: A human language used in oral and written communication.
example: An editor reviews Luxembourgish captions for a community video.

definition: A human language whose modern standard uses Cyrillic script.
example: A translator checks a Macedonian exhibit label.

definition: A human language used in speaking and writing.
example: A broadcaster records a Maithili public announcement.

definition: A human language used for conversation and written communication.
example: An interpreter explains appointment instructions in Malagasy.

definition: A human language written using the Malayalam script.
example: An editor reviews the Malayalam text on a school poster.

definition: A human language written with the Latin alphabet.
example: A translator prepares Maltese subtitles.

definition: A label for a set of Chinese varieties that includes the basis of Standard Mandarin.
example: A voice director requests a Standard Mandarin recording.

definition: A human language also called Meitei.
example: An educator checks the script and wording for a Manipuri reading exercise.

definition: A Goidelic human language associated with the Isle of Man.
example: A teacher records a short Manx conversation.

definition: A human language ordinarily written using Devanagari.
example: A translator checks a Marathi clinic handout.

definition: A numerical programming language and environment oriented toward arrays and matrices.
example: An engineer plots the frequency spectrum of a signal.

definition: A family of distinct languages, not one interchangeable language.
example: A translator specifies K'iche' rather than asking for an unspecified Mayan translation.

definition: An XML-based language for defining Windows Media Center interfaces and their behavior.
example: A developer describes how an interface element changes when it receives focus.

definition: A human language used in written and spoken communication.
example: An editor reviews Mizo text in a bilingual guide.

definition: A human language used in spoken and written communication across multiple script conventions.
example: A publisher specifies the intended script for a Mongolian edition.

definition: A programming language for indicators and automation in MetaTrader 4.
example: A developer computes a moving average for display on a price chart.

definition: A programming language with integrated persistent hierarchical data storage.
example: A maintainer retrieves an application record from a persistent global.

definition: An XML-based declarative language for describing interfaces in Apache Flex.
example: A developer declares a data-bound list in a Flex interface.

definition: A human language normally written using Devanagari.
example: A translator reviews a Nepali bus timetable.

definition: A statically typed compiled programming language with inference and metaprogramming facilities.
example: A developer uses a macro to generate repeated parsing code.

definition: A human language with Bokmål and Nynorsk written standards.
example: An editor prepares a Norwegian brochure in Nynorsk.

definition: A modular programming language in the Pascal tradition that supports type extension.
example: A developer defines an extended record type in an Oberon module.

definition: A language that extends C with object-oriented message passing.
example: A developer sends a message to an object in a legacy macOS application.

definition: A statically typed, functional-first language with algebraic data types and pattern matching.
example: A developer matches each possible form of an expression tree.

definition: A human language written using the Odia script.
example: An editor reviews Odia signage for a museum.

definition: A business application programming language integrated with the OpenEdge platform.
example: A developer validates a customer record before storing it.

definition: A multiparadigm programming language supporting dataflow concurrency and constraint programming.
example: A developer models a constraint that limits two events from sharing a time slot.

definition: A structured programming language with explicit types and procedures.
example: A learner uses a record to group student fields.

definition: A human language commonly written with an adapted Arabic script.
example: A translator checks the Pashto version of an enrollment notice.

definition: A general-purpose scripting language with strong text-processing capabilities.
example: An administrator extracts timestamps from log lines using a pattern.

definition: A human language with regional standards and varieties, including Iranian Persian, Dari, and Tajik.
example: A publisher specifies the intended Persian variety before commissioning narration.

definition: An ancient human language attested in inscriptions using the Phoenician alphabet.
example: An epigrapher transliterates a Phoenician inscription.

definition: A general-purpose scripting language commonly used to generate server-side web responses.
example: A developer renders a product page using records from a database.

definition: The seventh major generation of PHP, introducing features including scalar parameter and return type declarations.
example: A maintainer adds a return type to a PHP 7 function.

definition: A general-purpose programming language developed for both business and scientific computing.
example: A maintainer reads a PL/I program that handles fixed-format business records.
